full_reasoning:
Loop 1 of the position-tier-gate / full-trace arm. No prior loops — starting directly from the base algo. context_chars_in = 0.

Base algo (position-tier-gate) with position_cap=1: pnl=,262.50, sharpe=17.62, trade_count=90,433. The base mechanism serializes entry: any open position blocks the next open leg. This works extremely well vs simple baseline (+2,632%), suggesting the oracle signal quality at each individual entry is high, and the main source of edge destruction in the simple algo is simultaneous/rapid re-entries during noisy periods.

Hypothesis for loop 1: Try position_cap=2 (allow one additional concurrent position before gating). Reasoning: the base cap=1 is conservative — if the oracle fires 3 same-direction signals, only the first executes. The 2nd consecutive same-direction entry might carry valid directional information. A cap=2 loosening preserves most of the serialization benefit while allowing one additional concurrent contract.

Result: position_cap=2 is byte-identical to the simple baseline (pnl=, trade_count=136,734 = simple). This is a striking failure. The mechanism: the oracle fires simultaneous CLOSE+OPEN. When the OPEN arrives, the cache already shows 1 open position (the one that just closed but hasn't been processed by the fill engine yet). With cap=2, this OPEN (seeing 1 existing position < cap=2) is always submitted. The effect: cap=2 is a complete no-op — every OPEN passes through regardless of position state. cap=2 = simple baseline.

Key finding: The position_cap lever has a cliff between cap=1 (position_cap=1 = aggressive serialization = best operating point) and cap=2 (= simple = worst operating point). There is no smooth tradeoff between 1 and 2 for MES oracle with simultaneous CLOSE+OPEN signals. The oracle's simultaneous-signal structure makes any cap >= 2 equivalent to the simple baseline for this dataset.

Suggested next attempt: Since the position_cap lever is binary (1 = best, >=2 = worst), loop 2 should explore an entirely different mechanism. Candidates: (a) loss-streak gate (skip the next open after N consecutive losing closes); (b) time-since-last-close gate (minimum cooldown between close and next open, different from ptg-m-l1's cooldown which failed — that gated on time-since-last-submitted-open, not time-since-last-close); (c) flow-aware gate layered on top of the position gate (only submit when both position is flat AND flow is favorable).
